key_insight: The paper introduces a Turing-test-style evaluation for embodied world models that measures whether video foundation model predictions preserve human-perceived realism and remain robust under embodied interactions, revealing systematic gaps between generative video models and human expectations.
problem_solved: Establishes a standardized, human-centered benchmark to judge perceptual fidelity and robustness of predictive world models before applying them to downstream embodied tasks.
method: Design a Turing-test protocol where human evaluators try to distinguish real vs. model-predicted embodied video sequences.
Evaluate across diverse embodied scenarios, interaction horizons, and perturbations to probe generative generalization and robustness.
Combine human judgments with automated metrics to quantify fooling rate, fidelity, and failure modes for video foundation models.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical benchmark and evaluation protocol to diagnose whether video-based world models are perceptually convincing and resilient—guiding model selection, development priorities, and safe deployment in embodied systems.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: environment → agent action → model prediction → human evaluator (real vs. fake decision)
Bar chart: fooling rates or human error rates across different models/scenarios
Timeline/filmstrip: side-by-side ground-truth vs. predicted frames highlighting divergence points
Heatmap: robustness/fidelity scores across scenario types and perturbation strengths
paper_title: Wow, wo, val! A Comprehensive Embodied World Model Evaluation Turing Test
paper_authors: Chun-Kai Fan, Xiaowei Chi, Xiaozhu Ju, Hao Li, Yong Bao
